purpose: Replace the phenomenological shared c2 with concrete candidate physics under the separated TES/substrate joint model: (A) a finite real lead-lag readout section and (B) an additive downstream electronics-noise source that bypasses the Magnicon 10 kHz filter but is still shaped by the known 100 kHz hardware Bessel and first-alias fold.

real_lead_lag.semantics: one stable minimum-phase real zero/pole pair multiplying the documented Magnicon second-order Bessel response

bypass_electronics_noise.semantics: one shared white ASD source injected downstream of the Magnicon 10 kHz output filter but upstream of the known 100 kHz analog Bessel/sampling stage. The existing post-filter white ASD remains independently profiled per day.

guardrail: These are source-class replacement tests, not component identifications. The lead-lag family tests whether a finite real pole/zero pair can replace c2; if its pole runs high, the data only support a zero-like response. The bypass-noise family tests one specific source location: after the Magnicon 10 kHz filter but before the known 100 kHz hardware Bessel and sampling. A successful replacement does not prove that exact circuit location or noise source.
